Add an `f2c` (Fahrenheit to Celsius) command to the units CLI. Make one pull request that meets every acceptance line below.

Current state: `bin/units.js` handles only `c2f`. Any other command prints `unknown command: <cmd>` to stderr and exits 2. `src/convert.js` exports only `cToF`. `test/convert.test.js` tests `cToF`. `npm test` runs `node --test`. `README.md` has a `## c2f` section with an example.

Acceptance lines (all must hold):
1. `node bin/units.js f2c 212` prints `100` followed by a newline.
2. `node bin/units.js f2c 98.6` prints `37` followed by a newline.
3. `node bin/units.js c2f 100` still prints `212` followed by a newline.
4. `npm test` exits 0, and test/ contains at least one test of the Fahrenheit to Celsius conversion.
5. README.md documents f2c with an example invocation.

Steps:
1. In `src/convert.js`, add `fToC(f)` and export it next to `cToF`. Compute it as `(f - 32) * 5 / 9`. Do not use `(f - 32) / 1.8`: in Node it gives `36.99999999999999` for 98.6, which breaks line 2. `(98.6 - 32) * 5 / 9` gives exactly `37`.
2. In `bin/units.js`, add an `f2c` branch that prints `String(fToC(n))` with `console.log`, the same way `c2f` prints. Print plain numbers with no unit suffix. Leave the `c2f` branch, its output format, and the unknown-command message and exit status 2 unchanged.
3. In `test/convert.test.js`, or a new `*.test.js` file in `test/`, add tests for `fToC`. Assert at least that `fToC(212) === 100` and `fToC(98.6) === 37`. Keep the existing `cToF` test.
4. In `README.md`, add a `## f2c` section after `## c2f` with an example invocation in the same style, e.g. `    node bin/units.js f2c 212    # prints 100`.
5. From the repo root, run `node bin/units.js f2c 212`, `node bin/units.js f2c 98.6`, `node bin/units.js c2f 100` and `npm test`. Confirm the outputs are `100`, `37` and `212`, and that `npm test` exits 0.

Out of scope: Kelvin or any other unit, and any change to c2f output or to unknown-command behaviour.
